How to read the data

Before comparing numbers,
check the measurement basis.

01

Compare volumes within the same market

About 1.2 TWh of batteries were installed in electric vehicles worldwide in 2025, with LFP exceeding 55%. Fuel cells are usually measured by installed power (MW), while disposable cells may be counted by units, so these technologies are not ranked in one combined table. Sales and installed battery capacity are also different measures.

IEA source ↗
02

What does $/kWh price measure?

BloombergNEF's 2025 average pack prices were $108/kWh for all lithium-ion batteries, $81/kWh for LFP and $128/kWh for NMC. Cells, packs and installed systems are different products. Fuel cells are generators rather than energy-storage packs, so compare $/kW alongside fuel costs.

BNEF source ↗
03

Rare earths and critical minerals are different

Lithium, nickel, cobalt and platinum are not rare-earth elements. Some NiMH hydrogen-storage alloys contain rare earths such as lanthanum. USGS estimates 2025 lithium mine output at about 290,000 tonnes excluding the United States, but this cannot be converted directly into a maximum annual battery output. Refining, recycling, allocation between uses and material input per product all differ.

USGS source ↗

The categories group representative commercial, early-commercial and demonstration technologies. Lithium-polymer usually refers to cell construction and electrolyte form rather than a separate cathode chemistry. Data date: October 5, 2026. Prices are nominal USD and exclude exchange rates, retail markups and installation costs. Where comparable public figures could not be verified, this is stated explicitly.
